Answer: C
Reason: The chest radiographs show a large, lobulated soft-tissue mass in the anterosuperior mediastinum that appears to extend superiorly toward the neck (cervico-mediastinal), which is a characteristic presentation for a cervico-mediastinal well-differentiated liposarcoma. While thymomas and teratomas are common anterior mediastinal masses, the specific description of a lobulated cervico-mediastinal enlargement aligns best with this diagnosis among the choices provided.
